clue.text: Slow dance two finally moving in time

indicators.note: the closing pair of letters of the time word change places, so one of them shifts to the very end

parts.note: a minute is a unit of time; 'in' joins it to the moving instruction

explanation.surface: A stately dance in which two dancers finally step in time together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two finally moving' swaps the last two letters of MINUTE: lift out the T and put it back at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The minuet is a slow, graceful seventeenth-century court dance in triple time.

clue.text: Astronaut's pub used by key workers?

definitions.text: Astronaut's pub used by key workers?

parts.words: Astronaut's pub used by key workers?
parts.note: typists, who work at keys, all use the long key below the letters

explanation.surface: A bar in orbit frequented by essential workers.
explanation.definitionFit: The long bar on a keyboard that types a blank is pressed constantly by typists, the 'key workers'.

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, telling us to rearrange the letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A taste for poisoned liquor would be a strange thing to have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' signals an anagram of POISONED SPIRIT, all fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a natural inclination or tendency, which is what a leaning towards something amounts to.

definitions.meaning: excellent, as in a ... shot or ... regiment
the sharp noise of a gun going off

explanation.definitionFit: Crack means expert or top-notch, and is also the loud bang of a firearm.

clue.text: Engaged to keep old boys in order

definitions.text: Engaged to keep old boys in order

parts.words: Engaged to keep old boys in order
parts.note: a tailor engaged in advance to dress gentlemen makes clothes to individual order; the word also once meant arranged or booked ahead

explanation.surface: Someone hired to keep elderly men well behaved.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on two senses: arranged or engaged in advance, and tailored to order, as the made-to-measure suits of public-school old boys.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing made to a customer's individual order is described this way, and the old sense is spoken for or booked ahead.

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for money from right to left

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound note, British slang for a sum of money

explanation.surface: A gardener sells a plant to recoup cash.
explanation.walkthrough: A TENNER is British slang for a ten-pound note; 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Rennet is a name for a dessert apple variety and for lady's bedstraw, once used to curdle cheese.

parts.note: Gilbert and Sullivan's Pirates of Penzance would learn to seize ships; a school teaching that would train its pupils in boarding

explanation.surface: A school taking children from a Cornish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Penzance is a Cornish seaside town, but the question mark points to the comic opera The Pirates of Penzance: pirates board ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A school where pupils live during term is a residential school; pirates storm vessels by boarding them.

parts.note: a signalling system using outstretched arms, or held flags, as sailors of the volunteer reserve would wave

explanation.surface: Weapons, or messages sent by the naval reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wavy Navy was the nickname of the Royal Naval Volunteer Reserve, from the wavy gold braid on its officers' sleeves; 'wavy' also hints at arms waved in signalling.
explanation.definitionFit: A visual signalling code made by positioning the arms or two flags in set angles.

clue.text: Crime sheet stolen from the Parsonage

indicators.note: stolen from means taken away out of the vicarage word, so its letters are removed

parts.note: a parson's house, taken as written; that the crime also sits as a run inside it is a coincidence of removing the sheet word's scattered letters
a page is a single sheet of a book

explanation.surface: A bedsheet is pilfered from the vicar's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stolen from' removes PAGE, its letters scattered as P and AGE, from PARSONAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the criminal offence of deliberately setting fire to property.

indicators.note: modified means altered, telling us to rearrange the combined letters

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, meaning that is

explanation.surface: A workshop whose arrangements are changed at a later date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modified' rearranges IE and LATER together.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's studio, a place where creative work is made.

parts.note: something that bothers a few people but not everyone would vex only some of them

explanation.surface: A thing that bothers only certain people.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as IRKS OME, sounding like 'irks some': it annoys some people, not all.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiresome and vexing; the word splits as irks plus 'some', bothering a portion of people.

parts.note: E and N are the compass points east and north
to sue is to take legal action

explanation.surface: Obey instructions so that something gets done.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come after or result from something, as consequences do.

parts.note: having come out ahead financially, or, read literally, being a body of troops surrounded and isolated in a small enclosed area

explanation.surface: Turned a profit while isolated.
explanation.walkthrough: A pocket is also a small isolated area, such as encircled troops; being 'in a pocket' is being cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in profit after a deal is to have gained money; a pocket of resistance is a cut-off group.

clue.text: Game played from time to time

definitions.text: Game played from time to time

parts.words: Game played from time to time
parts.note: a lawn putting game where players move round twelve points marked like hours on a dial

explanation.surface: A pastime enjoyed only occasionally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from time to time' looks like 'occasionally', but in this lawn game the holes are set out like the hours on a dial, so play goes from one hour mark to the next.
explanation.definitionFit: A putting game on a circular lawn with twelve stations arranged like a dial face.

clue.text: Proof losing nothing by wrong diet — gained in fact

indicators.note: losing means the word for proof drops a letter

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

indicators.note: wrong means badly arranged, so the letters of diet are rearranged

explanation.surface: Evidence that a bad diet does nothing, and yet someone put on weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes one O from PROOF to give PROF; 'wrong' rearranges DIET as ITED. 'by' and 'in fact' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To have profited is to have benefited or made money from something.

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
signs here are pledges or tokens given as warranty

explanation.surface: Moves made against securities.
explanation.definitionFit: To consign something is to hand it over or deliver it into another's keeping.

clue.text: Heraldic colour a party displays in chapel

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
the Tories are the British Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A coat of arms in gold is shown by a political group in a chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic name for gold; TORY is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratory is a small private chapel used for prayer.

parts.note: a pliant willow twig of the kind woven into baskets, here imagined in a bread basket

explanation.surface: A shot fired into someone's stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breadbasket' is slang for the stomach, suggesting a gunshot; but the shoot is a willow twig woven into baskets.
explanation.definitionFit: A willow whose flexible young stems are used for basketwork.

clue.text: Service vow lies maybe in worship

parts.note: I do is the vow spoken at a wedding service

indicators.note: maybe suggests a possible version, telling us to rearrange the letters

explanation.surface: A wedding promise may be a falsehood in a place of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges I DO and LIES together. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To idolise someone is to admire or revere them excessively, as one would a god.

clue.text: In time it may save some pins

definitions.text: In time it may save some pins

parts.words: In time it may save some pins
parts.note: the proverb about one prompt bit of sewing saving nine, with 'nine' pins as in skittles

explanation.surface: Something done promptly saves a few pins.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'a stitch in time saves nine'; the clue swaps 'nine' for 'some pins', hinting at ninepins.
explanation.definitionFit: A single loop of thread in sewing, the subject of the proverb about prompt mending.

definitions.meaning: dealing in goods, often illicit ones

explanation.definitionFit: Traffic is vehicles that cause road jams, and also commerce or dealing, as in drug trafficking.

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the hyphenated word that follows

explanation.surface: A rapid boom in entertainment projects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points inside FUN-GIVING. 'schemes' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Mushrooms and toadstools spring up overnight, the proverbial sudden growth.
To take off clothes is to undress; a take-off is a mocking impersonation.

clue.text: Sort of square instrument for a pain in the side

parts.note: a T-square is the draughtsman's ruler, so T names that kind
a horn is a brass musical instrument

explanation.surface: A drawing tool or musical instrument that becomes a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: A T-square is a draughtsman's ruler shaped like a T. The definition comes from the idiom 'a thorn in the side'. 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A persistent irritation, from the idiom of a prickle lodged in one's flesh.

clue.text: His interest ranges far and wide

definitions.text: His interest ranges far and wide

parts.words: His interest ranges far and wide
parts.note: a student of mountains, whose subject is the great mountain chains

explanation.surface: A man with broad interests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ranges far and wide' reads as broad interests, but ranges are mountain chains, the subject of orology.
explanation.definitionFit: Orology is the scientific study of mountains, and a specialist in it studies ranges.

clue.text: Where actor may be third man on the farm?

definitions.text: Where actor may be third man on the farm?

parts.words: Where actor may be third man on the farm?
parts.note: the comic actor Will ..., perhaps in the cricket position third man, gives a meadow on a farm

explanation.surface: Where a performer plays a minor role on a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: Will Hay was a British comic film actor; third man is a cricket fielding position, so Hay would be in the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A meadow where grass is grown to be cut and dried as fodder.

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field
an end is a finish, a synonym for finally in noun form

explanation.surface: A cricket team is finally dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: The off side is the half of a cricket field facing the batsman's bat.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone out is to upset or annoy them, which is what giving offence does.
